attempted_claim: Let G be an infinite, pure, ω-categorical, characteristically simple p-group with NIP, for some prime p. Is G abelian? Equivalently, does Wilson's case (iii) — a non-abelian perfect p-group — occur under NIP?
decisive_failure: The unconditional virtually-nilpotent premise for omega-categorical NIP groups without fsg could not be established; only fsg-conditional nilpotent-by-finite, an unconditional infinite definable abelian subgroup, and generically-stable-conditional abelianness are available, and no original increment or auditable alternative emerged, so the Wilson case (iii) question under NIP remains open from this lane.
